Done. `out/T4/model.safetensors` is written and `out/T4/plan.yaml` holds the whole edit.

**Approach:** the plan loads all three checkpoints as aliases `base`/`ft1`/`ft2`, asserts the preconditions, then computes the merge in the algebraically equivalent form

```
base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base)  ==  0.2*base + 0.4*ft1 + 0.4*ft2
```

which sidesteps the ordering hazard entirely — neither task vector can be taken against an already-modified base. Float32 copies of the ft MLP tensors are created inside the `base` alias (so only one alias is written and output inference is unambiguous), `base`'s MLP tensors are cast to float32, scaled, accumulated, then cast back to float16 and the scratch tensors deleted.

**Checks in the plan:** 244 tensors in each input, 64 MLP tensors in each, every non-MLP tensor of ft1/ft2 bit-identical to base, MLP names mapping one-to-one, exactly 64 scratch tensors created (= merged), and 244 float16-MLP tensors with the non-MLP set untouched at the end.

**Three executions, two failures**, both my own assertions firing:
1. `equal` with `eps: 0.0` computes `|left-right|`, and `attention.masked_bias` is `-inf`, giving NaN — dropping `eps` uses bit-exact `torch.equal`.
2. The final dtype check covered all tensors, but `attention.bias` mask buffers are `uint8`, not float16 — narrowed to the merged tensors.

Independent verification of the output: 244 tensors, key set and dtypes match base, the 180 unchanged tensors bit-identical, worst relative Frobenius error over the merged tensors 2.4e-4 (limit 1e-3). Self-report is at `out/T4/REPORT.md`.
